scenes.title: A cache is a sticky note
scenes.narration: You look up a phone number in a thick book. The second time, you just read the sticky note you left on the fridge.

nodes.label: Sticky note
nodes.step: First you check the sticky note on the fridge. Quick!

nodes.label: Phone book
nodes.step: Not there? Look it up in the big phone book. Slow, but always right.

nodes.label: Write it down
nodes.step: Then write it on the sticky note, so next time is quick.

points: A cache is a small, fast copy of things you asked for recently. It can be out of date, so it forgets after a while.

scenes.title: How a cache fits in our story
scenes.narration: In Snip, Redis is the sticky note and Postgres is the phone book.

nodes.label: GET /Ab3x9Qz
nodes.step: A friend clicks the short link.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.step: Redis is checked first: the sticky note.

nodes.label: 302 redirect
nodes.step: Found there: off they go, without touching the database.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.step: Not there: Postgres, the phone book, has every link.

nodes.label: cache for 24h
nodes.step: Snip writes it on the sticky note for 24 hours, then redirects.

points: That 24-hour sticky note is why a deleted link can keep working for a day.
